name: Inguinal hernia
oneLine: A groin swelling with an expansile cough impulse, and the decision of who needs an operation tonight and who can wait for a planned repair

chapters.title: Basics
chapters.blurb: What a hernia is, and the three exits a groin hernia can take

chapters.title: Patient particulars
chapters.blurb: Age, sex and work set the prior probability before the groin is examined

skill.particulars.demographics.expect: In a groin swelling, age and sex point at the type before a finger is laid on. Indirect hernias favour the young and reach the scrotum; direct hernias favour older men with weak walls; femoral hernias favour older women and strangulate early. Heavy manual work and chronic straining complete the picture.

chapters.title: History of presenting illness
chapters.blurb: Tempo in years, the dragging ache, and what lying down does to the lump

skill.hx.chief_complaints.expect: A hernia history reads in months to years, not days: a groin lump noticed long ago, growing slowly, with a dragging ache that worsens through the day. Sudden severe pain in a previously quiet lump breaks that tempo and means complication until proved otherwise.

skill.hx.surg.lump.expect: Run the set questions for every inguinoscrotal swelling: how it started and on what strain, where it appeared first and where it travelled, its size when first seen, and whether it disappears on lying down. A lump that reached the scrotum at first sight grew into a preformed sac; one that started small and grew is acquired.

skill.hx.surg.groin_hernia.expect: Expect a swelling that comes on standing, coughing or lifting and goes on lying flat, with an aching drag rather than sharp pain. Ask about colic, vomiting, distension and absolute constipation for obstruction, and about bladder symptoms that change with the lump for a cystocele.

chapters.title: Past, personal, drug and family history
chapters.blurb: The pressure factors that must be treated or the repair fails

chapters.title: General examination
chapters.blurb: Usually a well patient; when he is not, the hernia has complicated

skill.gen.appearance.expect: The uncomplicated hernia patient looks well and walks in. A distressed, dehydrated patient with sunken eyes and a rigid abdomen has moved into obstruction or strangulation, and the groin is no longer the only examination that matters.

skill.gen.vitals.expect: Vitals are usually normal in an uncomplicated hernia, which is itself informative. Fever with tachycardia over a tense tender groin lump suggests strangulation with ischaemic bowel, while hypotension with distension suggests late obstruction: both change the urgency from routine list to tonight.

chapters.title: Groin and scrotal examination
chapters.blurb: Standing first, then the ring tests after reduction

skill.exam.surg.hernia_inspection.expect: Examine standing first with the groins exposed from umbilicus to mid thigh. An indirect hernia looks pyriform with a stalk at the external ring and runs to the scrotum; a direct hernia looks spherical and barely enters it. Reddened skin over the swelling means strangulation, and a large scrotal hernia pushes the penis aside.

skill.exam.surg.hernia_palpation.expect: Try to get above the swelling: impossible in inguinal hernia, possible in a pure scrotal lump. An enterocele feels elastic, is resonant and reduces with a gurgle; an omentocele feels doughy and granular, is dull and reduces without one. Tense tenderness with no impulse is strangulation, not a difficult reduction.

skill.exam.surg.deep_ring_occlusion.expect: Reduce the hernia first, press the thumb over the deep ring half an inch above the mid inguinal point, and ask the standing patient to cough. Silence under the thumb with no bulge is indirect and controlled; a bulge medial to the thumb is direct and unconcerned by the occlusion.

skill.exam.surg.invagination_three_finge.expect: After reduction, invaginate scrotal skin to the superficial ring and ask the patient to cough. An impulse on the tip of the finger travelling up, back and out is indirect; an impulse on the pulp striking straight back is direct. Zieman adds the third finger on the saphenous opening for the femoral orifice.

skill.exam.surg.scrotal_palpation.expect: In every inguinoscrotal swelling feel the testis apart from the hernia. A testis felt separate below the lump keeps hydrocele and tumour in mind; a testis impalpable within it fits a complete hernia or a large hydrocele, and an empty scrotum with a groin lump raises undescended or ectopic testis.

skill.exam.surg.transillumination_scrotu.expect: A hydrocele transilluminates brightly and a hernia does not, because bowel and omentum are opaque. Use the test to separate a tense complete hernia from a vaginal hydrocele when the scrotum is too full to feel through.

skill.exam.surg.regional_nodes.expect: Feel the groin nodes in every groin lump before calling it a hernia. Firm nodes with a foot or leg sore, an anal or genital lesion, or no obvious primary shift the diagnosis to lymphadenopathy, and an irreducible femoral lump with no cause found is settled in the theatre, not the ward.

stations.title: Examine the groin swelling
stations.task: This 48 year old farm labourer has had a right groin swelling for two years that descends into the scrotum. Examine his groin and scrotum and present your findings.
examinerQuestions: You cannot get above the swelling and it reduces with a gurgle. What does each finding prove?
After reduction you occlude the deep ring and ask him to cough, and a bulge appears medial to your thumb. Indirect or direct, and why?
The lump is tense, tender and irreducible with no cough impulse. How does your plan change?

stations.title: Take a hernia history and triage
stations.task: This 60 year old man has a groin swelling and worries it may need an operation. Take a focused history in six minutes and be ready to state whether this can wait for a routine list.
examinerQuestions: Which four chronic strains must you ask after before booking elective repair, and why does each threaten the repair?
He reports colicky pain, vomiting and absolute constipation with a now irreducible lump. What has happened and what do you do?
His swelling enlarges before micturition and shrinks after it, and pressure on it makes him want to pass urine. What does the sac contain?

skill.reasoning.inguinal.basics.title: What an inguinal hernia is
skill.reasoning.inguinal.basics.oneLine: Bowel through the groin wall, by one of three exits
skill.reasoning.inguinal.basics.why: The words direct, indirect and femoral are not labels but maps: they say where the bowel travels, whose groin it travels through, and where it is likely to get trapped. A student who knows the three exits reads every groin lump correctly; one who only knows the word hernia cannot.

teach.heading: A hernia is a protrusion, not a lump
teach.body:
A hernia is the protrusion of a whole viscus or part of one through the wall that contains it. The commonest herniae are abdominal: inguinal, femoral, umbilical, incisional and epigastric. Of these the inguinal hernia is by far the commonest groin hernia in both sexes and at all ages.

The inguinal canal carries the spermatic cord in men and the round ligament in women. An indirect hernia enters through the deep ring at the side of the inferior epigastric vessels and travels the canal; a direct hernia pushes through the weak posterior wall in Hesselbach triangle, medial to those vessels.

rows: Through the deep ring, along the canal, often to the scrotum
Young patients; almost all hernias in children and women
Narrow neck, so it can strangulate
Through the posterior wall medial to the deep ring, rarely far
Older men with weak abdominal walls
Wide neck, so it rarely strangulates
Through the femoral canal below the inguinal ligament
Older women, right side twice as often
Rigid narrow canal, so it strangulates readily

teach.heading: What the sac contains
teach.body:
Name the content and you have half the examination: an enterocele contains intestine, an epiplocele or omentocele contains omentum, and a cystocele contains bladder. The last occurs in direct or sliding hernias and declares itself when the lump swells before passing urine and shrinks after it.

Two rare traps share the same sac. In a sliding hernia the caecum, pelvic colon or bladder forms part of the sac wall itself. In Richter hernia only part of the bowel circumference is gripped, so obstruction signs stay deceptively mild while that knuckle of bowel dies.

teach.heading: Five clinical types, one ladder of urgency
teach.body:
A reducible hernia returns to the abdomen on lying down or with gentle taxis, though the sac stays behind. An irreducible hernia will not return but is otherwise quiet, held by adhesions or its own size. An obstructed or incarcerated hernia adds colic, vomiting, distension and absolute constipation without harming blood supply.

A strangulated hernia adds arrest of blood supply to irreducibility and obstruction: tense, tender, no cough impulse, skin going red. An inflamed hernia mimics it when an appendix or Meckel diverticulum inside the sac inflames, but it is not tense and has no obstruction. Climbing this ladder is the whole triage.

probes.q: Define a hernia, and name the commonest groin hernia.
probes.a: A hernia is protrusion of a viscus or part of one through the wall containing it, and the inguinal hernia is the commonest groin hernia in both sexes.

probes.q: How does the exit of a direct hernia differ from an indirect one?
probes.a: The indirect hernia enters through the deep ring lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels and travels the canal, while the direct hernia pushes through the weak posterior wall in Hesselbach triangle medial to those vessels.

probes.q: Why is a direct hernia less likely to strangulate than a femoral hernia?
probes.a: The direct hernia has a wide neck through a weak wall, so contents move freely, while the femoral hernia passes through a narrow rigid canal that grips its contents and arrests blood supply early.

sources.source: Bailey and Love's Short Practice of Surgery
sources.locator: Hernias: anatomy of the inguinal canal

skill.reasoning.inguinal.signs.title: The hernia picture
skill.reasoning.inguinal.signs.oneLine: Two classical signs, then contents, type and complications
skill.reasoning.inguinal.signs.why: Two signs diagnose an uncomplicated hernia, and every other manoeuvre only sorts what is inside it and which exit it took. A student who checks the two signs first never mistakes a strangulated hernia for a difficult reduction, because the signs themselves announce the emergency.

teach.heading: Impulse and reducibility come first
teach.body:
The two classical signs of an uncomplicated hernia are an expansile impulse on coughing and reducibility. Coughing drives more contents into the sac so the swelling expands against the fingers; lying down or gentle taxis returns them, and the sac stays behind.

Absence of an impulse does not exclude a hernia, because adhesions can block the neck, and a large femoral lump may barely move. But loss of a previously present impulse with a tense tender lump is never a difficult reduction: it is incarceration or strangulation.

rows: Resonant, bowel sounds may be heard
Gurgle; hard at first, easy at the end
No gurgle; easy at first, resists at the end
Pressure brings a desire to pass urine

teach.heading: Sorting indirect from direct
teach.body:
Three bedside facts separate them. The deep ring test, done standing after full reduction with the thumb over the ring, holds an indirect hernia back while a direct hernia bulges medial to the finger. The invagination test sends the finger up, back and out along the canal in indirect hernia and straight back in direct.

Zieman places three fingers at once: index on the deep ring, middle on the superficial ring, ring finger on the saphenous opening. The finger that feels the impulse names the orifice: indirect, direct or femoral. It works only with no obvious swelling or after complete reduction.

teach.heading: Strangulation announces itself
teach.body:
Call it strangulation when a lump is irreducible, without impulse, extremely tense and tender, with reddening skin. Obstruction follows with colic, vomiting, distension and absolute constipation, though a Richter hernia or a pure omentocele may obstruct late or never.

Never force taxis on such a lump: rough handling can return dead bowel to the abdomen or rupture it. Resuscitate, keep nil by mouth, and refer for urgent exploration the same day.

probes.q: Name the two classical signs of an uncomplicated hernia.
probes.a: An expansile impulse on coughing and reducibility of the swelling.

probes.q: How do you tell an enterocele from an omentocele at the bedside?
probes.a: The enterocele is elastic and resonant, reduces with a gurgle, and may show peristalsis or bowel sounds, while the omentocele is doughy and granular, dull to percussion, and reduces without a gurgle.

probes.q: What are the diagnostic features of a strangulated hernia, and what must you never do?
probes.a: Irreducible, no cough impulse, extremely tense and tender, often with reddened skin and obstruction features; never force reduction, because non-viable bowel may be returned to the abdomen.

sources.source: Browse's Introduction to the Symptoms and Signs of Surgical Disease

skill.reasoning.inguinal.differential.title: Differential diagnosis
skill.reasoning.inguinal.differential.oneLine: Femoral first, then the scrotal and groin mimics
skill.reasoning.inguinal.differential.why: Most groin lumps are hernias, but the ones that are not carry their own emergencies: a femoral hernia strangulates sooner, a torsion kills a testis in hours, and nodes point to disease elsewhere. The differential is not an academic list but the step that stops the wrong operation.

teach.heading: Inguinal or femoral comes first
teach.body:
Two landmarks settle it. An inguinal hernia lies above the inguinal ligament and medial to the pubic tubercle; a femoral hernia lies below the ligament and lateral to the tubercle, escaping through the saphenous opening. A large femoral lump can ride up over the ligament, so feel the base, not the dome.

Confirm with the canal: in femoral hernia the inguinal canal is empty on invagination, and pressure over the femoral canal holds the lump back. Remember that even in women the commonest groin hernia is still inguinal, so sex biases but never decides.

teach.heading: Scrotal swellings that are not hernia

rows: You can get above it; no cough impulse
Traction test: pulling the testis down fixes it
Fills from below; thrill, not expansile impulse
Lump is the testis itself in the canal or pouch
Painful cord with fever and rigors
Inflammatory, often filarial; cord tender throughout

teach.heading: Groin lumps below the ligament
teach.body:
Enlarged nodes demand a search from umbilicus to toes, including the anal canal, urethra and vagina, for the septic focus or malignant primary. The gland of Cloquet in the femoral canal can mimic an irreducible femoral hernia exactly, and without a cause the lump is settled in the theatre.

A saphena varix vanishes lying down and gives a fluid thrill rather than an expansile impulse, with varicose veins below and a tap impulse travelling up on Schwartz test. A psoas abscess points lateral to the femoral vessels with cross fluctuation and a diseased spine behind it; an aneurysm gives expansile pulsation, which no hernia ever does.

probes.q: How do you separate an inguinal hernia from a femoral hernia by surface anatomy?
probes.a: The inguinal hernia lies above the inguinal ligament and medial to the pubic tubercle, while the femoral hernia lies below the ligament and lateral to the tubercle.

probes.q: How do you tell a vaginal hydrocele from a complete inguinal hernia?
probes.a: In hydrocele you can get above the swelling, it fluctuates and transilluminates brightly with no cough impulse, while in hernia you cannot get above it and it carries an expansile impulse.

probes.q: A groin lump disappears lying down and gives an impulse on coughing, but so do two non-hernia conditions. Name them and how you tell.
probes.a: Saphena varix and varicocele both reduce lying down with a thrill-like impulse rather than an expansile one; the varix has varicose veins and a positive Schwartz tap test, and both refill gradually from below when the ring is held.

sources.source: Bailey and Love's Short Practice of Surgery
sources.locator: Hernias: differential diagnosis of groin swellings

skill.investigation.inguinal.workup.title: Confirming the hernia and grading its urgency
skill.investigation.inguinal.workup.oneLine: Hands first, ultrasound for doubt, bloods for the complicated
skill.investigation.inguinal.workup.why: A hernia is diagnosed by examination in standing and supine positions with a cough, not by a scan. Investigations exist for three narrower jobs: the lump you cannot feel, the hernia that has complicated, and the patient who must be fit for theatre.

teach.heading: The examination is the investigation
teach.body:
Expose both groins from umbilicus to mid thigh, examine standing first and then supine, and test the cough impulse, reducibility and the ring before ordering anything. Ordering a scan before this sequence wastes the one test that is always available and never wrong about strangulation.

Groin ultrasound earns its place when the swelling is uncertain, intermittent or clinically occult. CT or MRI with a strain view is reserved for complex, recurrent or occult hernias, and herniography is now rarely used. A scan never delays resuscitation and referral when the lump is tense and tender.

teach.heading: The complicated hernia needs bloods, not debate
teach.body:
When strangulation or obstruction is suspected, send baseline blood tests and lactate alongside resuscitation: a rising lactate with erythema of the skin or systemic sepsis points to ischaemic bowel inside the sac. These tests grade urgency; they do not decide it, because the tense tender irreducible lump has already decided.

Examine the abdomen for distension and obstruction in the same sitting, and keep the patient nil by mouth with a nasogastric tube if vomiting. Percussion helps at the bedside too: resonance favours a strangulated enterocele over acute funiculitis, which is dull.

teach.heading: Fitness for a planned repair
teach.body:
Elective mesh repair needs a fit patient more than a big workup: haemoglobin, urine routine, blood sugar, an electrocardiogram past middle age, and a chest radiograph in the chronic cougher. Control the cough, the constipation and the prostatic obstruction before the date, not after the recurrence.

In Indian practice these tests and the repair itself are available at most district hospitals and government medical colleges, often as day care surgery. Book the workup with the surgical outpatient visit so a farm labourer does not lose two days of wages to two separate trips.

probes.q: How is an uncomplicated inguinal hernia diagnosed?
probes.a: By clinical examination in standing and supine positions with cough impulse assessment and tests of reducibility, not by imaging.

probes.q: When do you order groin ultrasound, and when CT or MRI?
probes.a: Ultrasound when the swelling is uncertain or not clinically obvious, and CT or MRI for complex, recurrent or occult hernias.

probes.q: A hernia is tense, tender and irreducible with vomiting. What investigations do you send, and what must they not delay?
probes.a: Baseline bloods and lactate with resuscitation and abdominal assessment, and they must never delay urgent surgical referral and exploration for suspected strangulation.

sources.source: Bailey and Love's Short Practice of Surgery

skill.reasoning.inguinal.diagnosis.title: Diagnosis and triage
skill.reasoning.inguinal.diagnosis.oneLine: Name it completely, then decide tonight or routine list
skill.reasoning.inguinal.diagnosis.why: A diagnosis of hernia alone books nothing: the surgeon needs side, type, extent, contents and complications before deciding between a routine list and tonight. Triage is the diagnosis doing its real work, and it fails whenever strangulation is still on the table at midnight.

teach.heading: A complete diagnostic statement
teach.body:
State side, type, extent, contents and status in one line: an uncomplicated right indirect inguinal hernia, incomplete and reaching only to the mid scrotum, an enterocele, reducible with an expansile cough impulse. Each word earns its place: side directs the incision, type predicts the anatomy, extent predicts the dissection, contents predict the percussion.

Grade the lump against the ladder: reducible, irreducible, obstructed, strangulated or inflamed. A statement without that grade is unfinished, because the grade alone decides the urgency.

teach.heading: Triage: tonight or routine list
teach.body:
Tonight means resuscitate and explore: a tense tender irreducible lump with lost impulse, with or without obstruction, and any hernia with erythema, sepsis or a rising lactate. Obstruction without strangulation signs still admits the same day under close watch, because the third feature can arrive within hours.

Routine list means a reducible hernia with impulse intact, no obstruction and controlled pressure factors. Between them sits watchful waiting for the small minimally symptomatic hernia in a patient at high operative risk, with explicit safety-net advice on the symptoms that promote waiting to tonight.

teach.heading: What Nyhus adds to the plan
teach.body:
The Nyhus classification in the annexure grades the defect behind the lump: a normal ring with a sac, an enlarged ring, a posterior wall defect, and the femoral and recurrent defects. Higher grades and recurrences point to mesh and to a surgeon comfortable with the posterior wall.

Use it to counsel, not to impress. A child with a patent processus hears herniotomy without mesh and a quick return to normal activity; any adult, even a young adult with a simple indirect sac, hears tension-free mesh repair, and an older patient with a destroyed posterior wall hears of a longer dissection with honest talk about recurrence and chronic groin pain.

probes.q: Give a complete diagnostic statement for an uncomplicated right scrotal hernia with bowel inside.
probes.a: An uncomplicated right indirect inguinal hernia, incomplete and reaching only to the mid scrotum, an enterocele, reducible with an expansile cough impulse.

probes.q: Which findings move a hernia from the routine list to tonight?
probes.a: Irreducible with no cough impulse, tense and tender, with overlying erythema, obstruction features, sepsis or a rising lactate.

probes.q: An obstructed hernia has no strangulation signs at noon. Can it wait till morning?
probes.a: No. Admit the same day under close watch with resuscitation, because strangulation can supervene within hours and the cost of waiting is dead bowel.

skill.treatment.inguinal.management.title: Managing inguinal hernia
skill.treatment.inguinal.management.oneLine: Planned mesh repair for most, urgent operation for the strangulated few
skill.treatment.inguinal.management.why: A hernia never heals itself: the defect only enlarges and the neck only tightens. Elective mesh repair is safe and durable, while emergency surgery on strangulated bowel carries far higher morbidity, so the whole of management is getting the right patient to theatre at the right time.

teach.heading: Elective repair is the definitive treatment
teach.body:
Offer tension-free mesh repair for symptomatic hernias: the open Lichtenstein repair with polypropylene mesh secured to the inguinal ligament and conjoint tendon is the standard, and laparoscopic repair through the preperitoneal plane covers the whole groin floor, suiting bilateral and recurrent hernias.

In children the sac is the disease, so herniotomy, excision of the patent processus, suffices without mesh. Test the abdominal wall tone before choosing: a patient with grossly weak obliques and Malgaigne bulgings needs the stronger reconstruction, not the quicker one.

teach.heading: Watchful waiting, honestly offered
teach.body:
Consider waiting for a small minimally symptomatic hernia in a patient at high operative risk, never as neglect but as a reviewed decision. Waiting needs what surgery would have given: counsel on the low recurrence after mesh, and safety-net advice that a tense tender irreducible lump with vomiting means emergency, not the next review date.

A truss is not treatment. Long wear stains and thins the skin over the lump and atrophies the wall beneath, making the eventual operation harder. Discourage it except as a brief bridge where surgery must wait.

teach.heading: The strangulated hernia tonight
teach.body:
Resuscitate, keep nil by mouth, give perioperative analgesia and antibiotics by protocol, and explore urgently: open the sac, assess the bowel, and resect what is non-viable. Do not attempt taxis on any irreducible lump at the bedside: even a recently irreducible non-tender lump may harbour ischaemic bowel, and a tense tender strangulated hernia must never be squeezed back.

Address the cause in the same admission where possible. Repair means little if the patient returns to the same chronic cough, constipation or prostatic obstruction that built the hernia, so treat each before discharge.

teach.heading: Recovery and the Indian operating list
teach.body:
Advise against heavy straining while the wound heals, then return to light work early and to full lifting only after the surgeon reviews the wound. Warn every patient that chronic groin pain and recurrence, though uncommon after mesh, are the two complications worth naming beforehand.

Elective repair is available at government medical colleges and district hospitals, commonly as day care surgery. Ask the hospital help desk about current public insurance support for the admission, and give written return advice so a labourer from a distant village knows exactly when to travel back.

probes.q: What is the definitive treatment of a symptomatic inguinal hernia?
probes.a: Elective tension-free mesh repair, by open Lichtenstein or laparoscopic approach.

probes.q: When is watchful waiting reasonable, and what must accompany it?
probes.a: For a small minimally symptomatic hernia in a patient at high operative risk, with counselling and explicit safety-net advice on strangulation symptoms.

probes.q: A hernia is tense, tender and irreducible with vomiting. Outline management.
probes.a: Resuscitate, keep nil by mouth, give analgesia and antibiotics by protocol, and undertake urgent surgical exploration with resection of non-viable bowel; never force taxis on a strangulated hernia.

sources.source: Bailey and Love's Short Practice of Surgery

skill.treatment.inguinal.management.dosingNote: This module teaches management at the level of modality and principle: which hernias are repaired electively with mesh, which are watched, and which go to theatre tonight. Specific agents, routes and durations come from your current national or institutional guideline at the time of treatment. CliniX does not prescribe.

cases.title: A farm labourer with two years of groin swelling
cases.opening: Ramesh Patil, 48, has come to the surgical outpatient clinic with his wife. He walks in normally but keeps glancing down at a bulge in his right groin. Introduce yourself and take a history.
cases.fallback: I am not sure what you mean, doctor. Can you ask that a different way?

patient.name: Ramesh Patil
patient.residence: Rural, lives with his wife and three children

cues: what brings you here today
tell me about the swelling in your groin
what is the main problem today
presenting.reply: Doctor, since two years there is a swelling in my right groin. It comes down when I stand and goes away when I lie down to sleep.

cues: when did the swelling first appear
how did the lump start
has the swelling grown over time
lump_onset_course.reply: It started small in the groin two years back, after the harvest season of lifting heavy bundles. It has grown slowly since, and now it comes down into the scrotum.

cues: does the swelling go away on lying down
what happens to the lump when you lie flat
does the swelling disappear by itself
swelling_lying_flat.reply: Yes, as soon as I lie down at night it goes back by itself. In the morning when I stand up, it comes down again, especially if I cough.

cues: do you get pain in the groin
tell me about the dragging ache
does the swelling pain worsen through the day
groin_drag_pain.reply: There is a dragging ache in the groin by evening, after a full day in the fields. It is never sharp, and rest takes it away. Long before the lump came, I had this same ache.

cues: where did the swelling appear first
did the lump start in the groin or the scrotum
which side is the swelling on
lump_first_site.reply: It started in the right groin itself, above the crease, and travelled down into the scrotum over many months. The left side is completely fine.

cues: do you strain to pass stools
how often do your bowels move
do you suffer from constipation
bowel_constipation_habit.reply: Yes, for many years I pass hard stools every two or three days and must strain a lot. I have never shown anyone for this.

cues: do you pass urine frequently at night
do you wait for the urine stream to start
any difficulty in passing urine
urinary_prostate_flow.reply: I get up twice at night to pass urine, and the stream is slow to start. But the swelling does not change when I pass urine.

cues: do you have a long-standing cough
tell me about your morning cough
do you bring up sputum daily
chronic_cough_beedi.reply: I cough most mornings and bring up a little white sputum. I have smoked beedis since I was twenty, about a bundle a day.

cues: what work do you do each day
do you lift heavy weights at work
tell me about your farm labour
farm_lifting_work.reply: I am a farm labourer. In season I carry sugarcane bundles on my shoulder all day. There is no other work I know.

cues: how many beedis do you smoke
since when do you smoke beedis
do you chew tobacco as well
tobacco_beedi_use.reply: Only beedis, about one bundle daily for nearly thirty years. No chewing tobacco, and I drink only at festivals.

cues: have you had a hernia operation before
any earlier operation on the abdomen
were you ever operated for appendicitis
prior_repair_history.reply: Never, doctor. No operation of any kind, on this side or anywhere else.

cues: do you have diabetes or blood pressure
any heart or lung disease
any other illness I should know
other_illness_check.reply: No sugar, no blood pressure. I have never been admitted to hospital. I take no daily tablets.

cues: which medicines do you take every day
are you on any blood thinner tablets
do you take steroids regularly
daily_medicines_list.reply: Nothing daily, doctor. Only the paracetamol I took twice last month when the ache was more.

cues: has anyone in your family had a hernia
any groin operation in the family
does your brother have a similar swelling
hernia_family_tally.reply: My elder brother had the same swelling and was operated in the government hospital five years back. He is fine now.

cues: have you had colicky pain with vomiting
any swelling of the abdomen with constipation
has the lump ever become painful and stuck
redflag_bowel_block.reply: No, never. The lump has always gone back on lying down, and I have never vomited or had my stomach bloat up.

cues: does the swelling enlarge before passing urine
does pressure on the lump make you want to urinate
does the swelling shrink after micturition
bladder_size_change.reply: No such thing, doctor. Passing urine makes no difference to the swelling at all.

skill.gen.appearance.finding: A well built man in no distress, walking normally. No pallor, no breathlessness at rest, no guarding of the abdomen.

skill.gen.vitals.finding: Pulse 82 regular. Blood pressure 128/82. Respiratory rate 16. Afebrile. SpO2 98 percent on room air.

skill.exam.surg.hernia_inspection.finding: Standing: a pyriform right inguinoscrotal swelling running from above the groin crease to the mid scrotum, expanding visibly on coughing. Skin normal, no redness, no scar. The penis is pushed to the left. Left groin flat.

skill.exam.surg.hernia_palpation.finding: Cannot get above the swelling at the root of the scrotum. Elastic in feel, non-tender, with an expansile impulse on coughing. Reduces on lying down with a gurgle; resonant to percussion over the lump.

skill.exam.surg.deep_ring_occlusion.finding: After full reduction, pressure over the right deep ring controls the hernia completely: no bulge appears on coughing while the thumb holds.

skill.exam.surg.invagination_three_finge.finding: Invagination reaches a roomy superficial ring. Cough impulse felt on the tip of the finger, travelling up, back and out along the canal. No impulse on the ring finger over the saphenous opening.

skill.exam.surg.scrotal_palpation.finding: Right testis felt separately below the reduced lump, normal in size and feel. Left testis and cord normal. No cord thickening, no varicocele.

skill.exam.surg.transillumination_scrotu.finding: The scrotal swelling does not transilluminate.

skill.exam.surg.regional_nodes.finding: No inguinal or femoral nodes felt on either side. No foot or leg sore, no genital lesion.

usg_groin.label: Ultrasound of the right groin
usg_groin.result: Defect in the right inguinal canal with bowel loops entering the sac on straining, reducing at rest. No free fluid, no thickened bowel wall, no collection. Left groin normal.
usg_groin.note: Confirms the clinical diagnosis and the contents, and excludes a complicated sac before a planned repair.

hb.label: Haemoglobin and full blood count
hb.result: Haemoglobin 13.8 g/dL. Total leucocyte count normal with a normal differential.
hb.note: Fitness baseline for elective surgery; no anaemia, no leucocytosis to suggest inflammation or strangulation.

urine.label: Urine routine
urine.result: No albumin, no sugar, no pus cells.
urine.note: Routine fitness test before mesh repair; infection of urine would postpone an implant.

sugar.label: Fasting blood sugar
sugar.note: Undiagnosed diabetes worsens wound healing around mesh, so it is checked even without symptoms.

ecg.label: Electrocardiogram
ecg.result: Normal sinus rhythm, no ischaemic changes.
ecg.note: Fitness for anaesthesia nearing fifty; his beedi years make a baseline tracing worthwhile.

cxr.label: Chest radiograph
cxr.result: No active lung lesion. Mild chronic bronchitic markings.
cxr.note: Ordered for the morning cough and beedi history, to grade the chest before anaesthesia rather than to diagnose the hernia.

ct_groin.label: CT of the groin
ct_groin.note: Not indicated: the hernia is clinically obvious with a clear cough impulse and reducibility, and ultrasound already mapped the sac. Reserve cross-sectional imaging for recurrent or occult hernias.

doppler_scrotum.label: Scrotal Doppler
doppler_scrotum.note: Not indicated: the testis is felt separately, there is no acute pain, and nothing suggests torsion or a varicocele needing flow study.

differentialModel.answer: Right indirect inguinal hernia, uncomplicated. Consider a direct inguinal hernia, a femoral hernia, a vaginal hydrocele, a varicocele, inguinal lymphadenopathy, a saphena varix and a lipoma of the cord.

diagnosis.answer: Uncomplicated right indirect inguinal hernia, incomplete and reaching only to the mid scrotum, an enterocele, reducible with an expansile cough impulse.

managementModel.answer: Book elective tension-free mesh repair with fitness workup, treat the constipation, beedi cough and prostatic symptoms first, give written safety-net advice on strangulation, and counsel on lifting and review after surgery.

teachingPoints: The tempo alone points to hernia before a finger is laid on: two years of a lump that comes on standing and goes on lying down is a mechanical story, not an infective or malignant one.
Two signs make the diagnosis: an expansile cough impulse and reducibility with a gurgle. Resonance and the gurgle together say the sac holds bowel, an enterocele.
Deep ring occlusion holding the hernia back plus an impulse on the fingertip travelling up, back and out marks this as indirect, not direct.
Normal vitals and a well patient are findings, not gaps: they place this hernia on the routine list rather than tonight, which is exactly what triage must state.
The constipation, beedi cough, nocturia with hesitancy and daily lifting are not background: each is a pressure factor that must be treated or the repair fails.
A hydrocele would let you get above it and would transilluminate; nodes would need a primary sought from umbilicus to toes. Their negatives here are doing real diagnostic work.
Ultrasound confirms and maps; it never replaces the ring tests. CT and Doppler were correctly left unordered, and restraint with tests is part of the lesson.
